page: Amazon Web Services m8gd.metal-48xl is a bare-metal, general-purpose instance powered by AWS Graviton4 Neoverse-V2 processors. Built on the 64-bit ARMv9 architecture, the server delivers 192 dedicated physical cores clocked at 2.7 GHz with a single thread per core. Memory capacity totals 768.0 GB of DDR5 RAM, maintaining a balanced ratio of 4.0 GB per core. The configuration includes 11,400 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 50 Gbps, with zero integrated GPUs.

Benchmark results demonstrate exceptional multi-core scalability and high data-throughput capabilities. The server achieves top-tier scores in multi-core metrics, including stress-ng multi-core CPU testing (298,073.2) and Geekbench multi-core performance (21,219.0), bolstered by massive memory read bandwidth reaching 895.56 GB/sec on uncached 256MB blocks. It excels in parallel execution profiles like Clang compilation (86,345.0) and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression (1,311.49 GB/sec). Storage and throughput testing show top-tier execution in database operations (45,871.95) and Redis SET benchmarks (391.52 million operations/sec), alongside 150.44 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

Single-core performance presents a distinct tradeoff, scoring in the mid-range across stress-ng single-core (1,648.69) and Geekbench single-core (1,663.0) suites. Additionally, LLM text generation metrics consistently fall into the lower quartile (such as 6.55 tokens/sec on 7B models and 2.64 tokens/sec on 70B models), reflecting the absence of discrete GPU acceleration despite strong CPU-based prompt processing speeds. Cost efficiency is driven primarily by resource density, pairing massive parallel compute with expansive low-latency NVMe scratch space on a single bare-metal host.

Given its hardware specifications, Amazon Web Services m8gd.metal-48xl is best suited for parallel enterprise workloads requiring high memory bandwidth, multi-threaded CPU power, and fast local disk access. Primary target deployments include in-memory databases, large-scale Redis caching arrays, high-throughput static web serving, Clang compilation pipelines, and transactional database systems.
